title: Transfer Fees on Returned and Recalled Payout Methods Transfers
content:
What became of a Payout Methods transfer decides how its discounted transfer fee is charged. A transfer returned at most 10 calendar days after it was sent was rejected on arrival, and half of the discounted transfer fee is charged; a transfer returned later than that had to be traced and recalled through the correspondent banks, and the discounted transfer fee is charged in full with a trace charge of USD 12.00 added to it; a transfer that settled is charged the discounted transfer fee as it stands. Nothing is rounded until that last step, which is rounded half up to the cent.

## Reading the ledger

- **The transfer.** The transfer the fee names, with the date it was sent.
- **Its return.** A return entry on the method's ledger naming that transfer, with the date of the return. No such entry means the transfer was not returned.
- **Days.** Calendar days from the date the transfer was sent to the date of its return.

## Outcome table

| What became of the transfer | Transfer fee charged |
|---|---|
| Returned 0 to 10 calendar days after it was sent (rejected on arrival) | Half of the discounted transfer fee |
| Returned more than 10 calendar days after it was sent (traced and recalled) | The discounted transfer fee in full, plus a trace charge of USD 12.00 |
| Not returned (settled) | The discounted transfer fee as it stands |

## Both sides of the 10-day line (hypothetical transfer sent 2026-07-13, discounted transfer fee USD 15.00)

| Return date | Calendar days | Transfer fee |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-23 | 10 | Half of USD 15.00: USD 7.50 |
| 2026-07-24 | 11 | USD 15.00 plus USD 12.00: USD 27.00 |
| No return | — | USD 15.00 |

## Further illustration (hypothetical)

A discounted transfer fee of USD 13.35 on a transfer returned 4 calendar days after it was sent: half is USD 6.675, rounded half up at the last step to USD 6.68. The trace charge is added after the discount and is not itself discounted.
